correctedState: The finding stands as written; three refinements. (a) Our '!' mode is not merely 'stuck on the pre-change behavior' by omission — the pre-change behavior is PINNED BY A TEST. sessions.shell-command.test.ts:148-180 asserts the executed command produces exactly one appended user message and one user_message event and nothing further, so implementing the new default means changing a green contract test, not just adding a branch. (b) The escape hatch would not literally be `respondToBashCommands` in `settings.json` in this fork. Nessy's own preference surface is packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts (schema + validators + config-defaults.json), and settings.json here is the Claude-compatibility store (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-settings-store.ts) used for permissions/managed policy, not for composer UI behaviour. The correct parity target is a Nessy config key with the documented default (respond = true) plus an opt-out, matching the fork's config-naming convention — the behaviour is the contract, the key location is not. (c) One adjacent divergence the row does not mention, worth carrying with it: our '!' mode also refuses to run at all in explore and plan permission modes (SessionManager.ts:16393-16402) and prompts for permission in default mode (:16416-16421), neither of which Claude's shell mode does. That is a separate, deliberate-looking hardening, not part of this gap, but anyone implementing the respond-by-default change will touch the same function and should not silently drop it.
